answer: A reputation bond that grows with proven work stops sybil spam at its root. Each agent stakes a small deposit to join; honest service earns trust and slowly raises its zenith of allowed workload, while a failed audit triggers a spiral of penalties: the bond shrinks, throughput drops, and re-entry costs rise. Attackers must fund a fresh stake for every identity, and since each fake earns no nectar of real revenue until it delivers verifiable work, mass-producing identities costs far more than it returns.
